fields.title: Coronary artery disease
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Coronary artery disease is a chronic condition that develops when the heart muscle does not receive enough blood. It arises from the build-up of atherosclerotic plaques that narrow the blood vessels and limit the flow of oxygen to the heart. This leads to chest pain (angina) and can progress to a heart attack. It is important to diagnose and treat coronary artery disease in good time in order to prevent serious complications. In this article we describe the methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of treatment in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis plays a decisive part in establishing the extent of damage to the heart and planning treatment. Modern diagnostic methods include:

  • Electrocardiography (ECG): a simple and quick method that records the electrical activity of the heart. In coronary artery disease an ECG may show abnormalities of rhythm or changes associated with ischaemia.
  • Stress testing: carried out during physical exertion to assess the heart's response to exercise and identify problems with the blood supply.
  • Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): produces detailed images of the heart and allows its structure and function to be assessed.
  • Coronary angiography: an invasive method in which a contrast medium is introduced into the blood vessels to image the coronary arteries and assess their condition.

Methods of treatment

Treatment aims to improve the blood supply to the heart and prevent the disease progressing. It may include:

  • Drug therapy: medicines such as antiplatelet agents, beta blockers and nitrates are used to control symptoms and reduce the risk of complications.
  • Percutaneous coronary intervention: catheters are used to widen the narrowed arteries and place stents to restore normal blood flow.
  • Surgery: in some cases coronary artery bypass grafting may be needed, in which grafts are placed to bypass the narrowed sections of the arteries.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is a world leader in cardiology and cardiovascular surgery and offers advanced treatment for coronary artery disease. The advantages include:

  • Qualified specialists: Israeli cardiologists and surgeons are highly qualified and have extensive experience in treating coronary artery disease.
  • Use of advanced technology: medical institutions in Israel are equipped with modern technology, which ensures a high level of professionalism and good treatment results.
  • An integrated approach to treatment: Israel takes a whole-person approach to coronary artery disease, which allows patients to receive comprehensive and individual care.

Conclusion

Coronary artery disease is a serious condition that requires comprehensive treatment and follow-up by experienced specialists. Modern methods of diagnosis and advanced approaches to treatment make Israel an attractive place to deal with it. If you have symptoms of coronary artery disease, consult a doctor for timely diagnosis and effective treatment to protect the health of your heart and improve your quality of life.

fields.title: Pacemakers and coronary angiography
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Pacemakers and coronary angiography are two modern and effective methods of diagnosing and treating heart disease. Pacemakers are used to regulate the heart rhythm, while coronary angiography allows the state of the heart's blood vessels to be assessed and any narrowing or blockage identified. In this article we describe the methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of using pacemakers and coronary angiography in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

  • Pacemakers: electronic devices fitted under the skin of the chest. They monitor the heart rhythm, correct arrhythmias and prevent the heart stopping.
  • Coronary angiography: an invasive procedure in which a contrast medium is introduced into the blood vessels of the heart so that the coronary arteries can be seen on X-ray images. This establishes whether there is narrowing or blockage, and how severe it is, which could lead to a heart attack.

Methods of treatment

  • Pacemakers: used to treat various types of arrhythmia and heart block. They may be fitted temporarily or permanently, depending on the patient's condition.
  • Coronary angiography: where narrowing or blockage is found in the coronary arteries, further procedures can be carried out to treat them. These may include stenting (placing a stent to widen the vessel) or coronary artery bypass grafting (fitting an arterial or venous graft).

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Qualified specialists: medical institutions in Israel have experienced and highly qualified cardiologists and surgeons who specialise in pacemakers and coronary angiography.
  • Use of advanced technology: doctors in Israel use advanced medical equipment and technology to diagnose and treat heart disease, which ensures a high level of accuracy and good results.
  • An integrated approach to treatment: Israel takes a whole-person approach to heart disease, which allows patients to receive individual and comprehensive treatment.

Conclusion

Pacemakers and coronary angiography are important innovative methods of diagnosing and treating heart disease. In Israel, highly qualified specialists and advanced technology make these procedures more effective and safer. If you have problems with your heart, consult a qualified cardiologist in Israel for the best treatment and to restore the health of your heart.

fields.title: Cataract
fields.bodyHtml:
A cataract is a clouding of the lens of the eye that leads to deteriorating vision. It is one of the most common eye conditions in people over 60, although it can also occur in younger people following injury or other illness.

Diagnosis of cataract

  1. Visual examination: the doctor examines the eyes using a slit lamp to assess the state of the lens and identify any clouding.
  2. Tonometry: measurement of the pressure inside the eye to rule out glaucoma, which can accompany a cataract.
  3. Visual acuity tests: used to establish the degree of sight loss and how the cataract affects the patient's daily life.
  4. Ultrasound scanning: carried out to obtain an accurate image of the structures of the eye and assess the state of the lens.
  5. Optical coherence tomography (OCT): produces high-quality images of the retina and optic nerve in order to rule out associated conditions.
  6. Keratometry and biometry: measurement of the curvature of the cornea and the length of the eye for accurate selection of the intraocular lens.

Methods of treating cataract

  1. Phacoemulsification:
    • The most widely used surgical treatment for cataract. The surgeon uses ultrasound energy to break up the clouded lens, which is then removed through a small incision. An artificial intraocular lens is then fitted.
    • Advantages: minimal injury to the tissues of the eye, rapid recovery, minimal risk of complications.
  2. Laser cataract surgery:
    • The use of a femtosecond laser to make precise incisions and break up the lens. This method improves the accuracy and safety of the operation.
    • Advantages: high precision, minimal risk of complications, shorter operating time.
  3. Extracapsular cataract extraction (ECCE):
    • A method in which the clouded lens is removed while the capsular bag is left in place for the intraocular lens. Usually used in advanced cataracts.
    • Advantages: allows the removal of large cataracts and stable placement of the lens.
  4. Intracapsular cataract extraction (ICCE):
    • A method in which the whole lens is removed together with the capsular bag. Rarely used, usually in complicated cataracts.
    • Advantages: allows treatment of difficult cases where other methods are unsuitable.

Advantages of cataract treatment in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: Israeli ophthalmologists have great experience and are recognised worldwide for their work in treating cataracts.
  2. Modern equipment: clinics are equipped with the newest diagnostic and surgical devices, which ensures accuracy and effectiveness.
  3. An individual approach: every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of all aspects of their health.
  4. A short recovery period: thanks to modern technology and techniques, recovery is quick and causes the patient minimal discomfort.
  5. High standards of safety and quality: Israeli clinics adhere strictly to international protocols and standards of medical care.

Cataract treatment in Israel gives patients access to highly qualified medical care, improves their sight and allows them to return to an active life.

fields.title: Ovarian cysts
fields.bodyHtml:
Ovarian cysts: advanced treatment in Israel

Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs in the ovaries and are common in women of reproductive age. Most ovarian cysts are functional and resolve on their own, but some may require medical treatment, particularly if they cause painful symptoms or pose a risk to health. The newest methods of diagnosing and treating ovarian cysts are available in Israel.

Diagnosis of ovarian cysts:

  1. Transvaginal ultrasound:
    The main method of diagnosing ovarian cysts, allowing their size, structure and exact position to be assessed.
  2. Laboratory tests:
    Blood tests for hormones and tumour markers such as CA-125 may be carried out to assess the nature of the cysts and rule out malignancy.
  3. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used for more detailed imaging, particularly in unclear cases or where cancer is suspected.
  4. Laparoscopy:
    A minimally invasive procedure sometimes used both to diagnose and to remove cysts.

Methods of treating ovarian cysts:

  1. Observation: many functional cysts resolve on their own, and doctors may recommend periodic follow-up with repeat ultrasound scans to monitor their size and condition.
  2. Hormone therapy: oral contraceptives or other hormonal medicines can help reduce the likelihood of new cysts forming and limit the growth of existing ones.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Cystectomy: removal of the cyst with preservation of the ovary.
    • Oophorectomy: removal of the whole ovary may be recommended where a cyst appears suspicious or where other conditions such as endometriosis are present.
    • Laparoscopic surgery: the preferred minimally invasive method of removing cysts, which shortens recovery and reduces pain after the operation.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • Advanced medical equipment and highly qualified specialists: Israeli clinics are equipped with the latest medical technology, and the doctors have extensive international experience.
  • An individual approach: every patient is offered a personalised treatment plan that takes account of her particular medical and personal needs.
  • A multidisciplinary approach: gynaecologists work with radiologists, endocrinologists and oncologists to ensure comprehensive care.

Treatment of ovarian cysts in Israel is aimed at dealing with the problem as effectively and safely as possible while preserving a woman's reproductive health and minimising any adverse consequences.
